newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut's B.Audi shares strong despite dividend.
newsitem.headline: Beirut's B.Audi shares strong despite dividend.

text.p: Shares of Banque Audi, the star of the Beirut Stock Exchange recently, performed strongly on Tuesday despite going ex-dividend.
Banque Audi announced that its shareholders approved a 40 cents dividend on Monday, the first it has issued. It will be paid on March 3 to shareholders on the registry on February 24.

The shares traded at $17 on Tuesday compared with $17.25 on Monday but brokers said the fact that the difference was less than the 40 cents dividend indicated that the shares were actually up on the day.
Shares which go ex-dividend are normally quoted at the price of the previous day's close less the amount of the dividend. In Banque Audi's case this would have put the price at $16.85, brokers said.
Turnover in Banque Audi rose to 31,427 from 10,850 on Monday. This included a block trade of 18,900 shares at $17 on the floor of the bourse.

Banque Audi executive Freddie Baz told Reuters the dividend represented a 30 percent payout ratio and a 2.5 percent dividend yield. "This is very respectable and is good by international and regional standards," Baz said.
Banque Audi shares have risen steadily since their January 20 debut at $15 on the Beirut market.
The other listed bank share -- Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce -- was unchanged at $12.625.
Some 11,000 BLC shares were traded, down from Monday's 15,000.
Solidere A was unchanged from $10.5 while B shares fell to $10.875 from $11.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Uniceramic and Eternit.
Total BSE turnover was 89,305 shares for a value of $1,167,454.5 from Monday's 77,094 and $918,410.5.
The BLOM index dropped 0.39 percent to 909.33 and the LISPI stock index fell 0.26 percent to 81.55.
